public_rationale: TotalRecall's June 6, 2024 extraction example, preserved in documentation updated June 8, demonstrates readable screenshot-derived text in an SQLite database without separate database encryption [e1]. Independent testing published June 4 verified access to raw Recall data in Windows 11 24H2 build 26100.712 [e2]. Whole-disk encryption could protect the stored files, but Ars Technica reported that it was generally enabled by default when signed into a Microsoft account [e2]. This supports disk-level protection without establishing that it required a separate manual choice [e2].
limitations: The tests concern an early preview implementation; they do not establish the protections in later Recall releases [e1, e2].
The evidence establishes readable SQLite contents, not that the database was literally a plain-text document [e1, e2].
The evidence does not establish that whole-disk encryption required explicit manual configuration [e2].
The technical evidence does not settle the post's conflicting chronology or its subjective security characterizations.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: It has come out that the database indexing Microsoft Recall's screenshots is stored in plain text, except on systems explicitly set to encrypt everything, which Marcus calls bananas and Keystone Kops level security.
conditions: except on systems that are explicitly set to encrypt everything

statement.excerpt: Two weeks later, it has already come out that the database that indexes the whole thing is in plain text (except on systems that are explicitly set to encrypt everything). That’s bananas. Keystone Kops level security.
statement.document_title: The misguided backlash against California’s SB-1047

from_speaker: Two weeks later, it has already come out
the database that indexes the whole thing is in plain text
except on systems that are explicitly set to encrypt everything
our_interpretation: Assess the early Recall implementation examined around the post date, not later redesigned releases.
Plain text means readable, unencrypted database contents, not that the SQLite file is literally a plain-text document.
Read the exception as referring to whole-disk encryption, which is distinct from encryption applied to the database itself.
Use May 24 through June 7, 2024, reflecting the post's recent two-week context. Its reference to March 24 conflicts with that context.
The descriptions bananas and Keystone Kops level security are opinions; the assessable proposition is the database's storage protection.
criteria.support_condition: Direct technical examination of the relevant early Recall implementation establishes that its screenshot-derived text index was readable in an SQLite database without separate database encryption, while system-level disk encryption could protect the stored files.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Direct examination establishes that the relevant early implementation independently encrypted its index database, or that the plaintext reports concerned a different product or materially different implementation.
